issues.description: Close message type contradicts the stated specification.
issues.detail: The PR description and linked Deepgram docs require {"type": "CloseStream"}. The code sends {"type": "Close"}. The precondition for graceful closure — that the server recognize the control message — is therefore not established. This is the exact bug the PR claims to fix, restated under a different name. REFUSED until the literal matches the spec.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() does not satisfy the postcondition of draining remaining audio.
issues.detail: Postcondition claimed: "all remaining audio is processed and all transcripts/audio are returned." The implementation awaits exactly one frame with a 1s timeout, then closes. There is no invariant relating frames-received to frames-expected, no termination function, no loop. The author cannot state when the drain is complete; they have hoped, not reasoned. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE for stating which failures are admissible.
issues.detail: The try/except swallows every exception from send_str and the inner wait_for, logs a warning, and proceeds to close. The author has not enumerated which exceptions are expected (ConnectionResetError, WebSocketError) versus which indicate program-logic faults. A blanket catch is a smuggled goto into the finally clause and hides real bugs behind a polite log line.

issues.description: Sending Flush before Close is unjustified by the cited specification.
issues.detail: The PR text and linked references describe only CloseStream. The Flush message is introduced without precondition, without postcondition, and without an argument for why both are required when one would suffice. Either Flush is necessary — in which case state why — or it is cargo, in which case remove it. Elegance is not optional.

review.summary: The patch attempts to fix a real bug — ungraceful WebSocket termination — but does so by substituting a different ungraceful termination. The control message sent is `{"type": "Close"}` while both the PR description and Deepgram's documentation require `{"type": "CloseStream"}`; the author has not checked that their literal matches their specification. The drain step is a single receive with a 1-second timeout and no invariant tying it to the postcondition of "all remaining audio processed." A bare `except Exception` is used in place of stating which failures are admissible. REFUSED until the message literal is corrected and the drain has a stated termination condition.
